As the new school year begins, more and more Americans are expressing support for banning students from using mobile phones throughout the entire school day.

The new school year officially starts, and support for banning iPhones in classrooms continues to rise

Yes, although it is still July, summer vacation has somehow already ended. My children are going back to school today and tomorrow, marking the second consecutive year that the first day of school is not in August.

Apple has launched its annual "Back to School" promotion to coincide with the season. Eligible students and educators who purchase selected Mac and iPad models before August 27 can receive a gift card of up to US$150. Consumers in several states can also enjoy limited-time sales tax holiday offers.

Although back-to-school discounts are welcome, the use of smartphones during class hours is increasingly unpopular.

The most liked comment was posted by Steve

I have not seen any data supporting the idea that allowing students to use mobile phones during school shooting incidents can reduce risk. In everyday reality, reducing distractions during class is the only way to truly fulfill the original purpose of attending school.

A recent survey by the Pew Research Center shows that 77% of American adults support banning middle and high school students from using mobile phones during class hours. This is up from 68% in 2024 and 74% in 2025, with only 18% currently opposing classroom bans.

Support for stricter, full-day bans on mobile phone use from class to dismissal is rising even faster. For the first time, more Americans support rather than oppose banning mobile phones throughout the entire school day.

The report also noted that support for classroom bans and full-day bans remains lower among young people, although support has risen across all age groups since 2024. The full report can be read here.

What do you think? Should schools restrict iPhone use only during class hours, enforce a full-day ban from class to dismissal, or leave the decision to students and parents? Feel free to share your views in the comments section.
